- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

<function call omitted for brevity>

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. - pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request

- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit

- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `SFCC-196` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #59** (component + CSS layer,
  focused vs shared recipes) and **PR #56** (the token layer).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are
  under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/`. No repo file is touched — not one.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CODEOWNERS`, `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. All Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never infer squad ownership** from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. They contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Never present a gap as resolved because it seems minor.** Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Say what you did not check.** A source you skipped is itself a finding.
- **Provenance, not proximity.** A document living in the codebase is a downstream artifact, not
  a source. If you cannot locate the original source for a claim, flag it **provenance unknown**
  and ask. Never fabricate a source, and never fall back to citing a codebase path as one.
- **Local-only docs are never citable.** `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are
  Marcel's personal files. **They must never appear in a PR, a commit message, or a code
  comment.** Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite the repo file
  instead — that is the citable source.
- **Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full treatment. At `quick` depth,
  drop the exemplar-PR read and the blast-radius sweep, and keep the gate. Nothing too crazy,
  no overthinking.

I'll run this at **`standard`** depth (the default — say if you want `exhaustive`).

**Phase 0 — position.**

   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |

1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

The storefront (PWA Kit on MRT) requires a mechanism to limit the quantity of any given product variant a shopper can purchase in a single order. This limit must be manageable by merchandisers without requiring a code deployment. The global maximum acts as the baseline fallback; per-product and per-customer-group overrides are addressed in SFCC-703.

### 1.2 Problem

There is currently no site-level configuration in Business Manager that defines a global maximum purchase quantity per variant. Without this, the enforcement logic planned for the PDP (SFCC-196) and Cart (SFCC-250) has no config source to read from, making those tickets unbuildable. The configured value must be available to the PWA Kit storefront via the SCAPI product response.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

SFCC-196 and SFCC-250 are blocked — neither PDP nor Cart enforcement can be implemented without a config source. Merchandisers have no ability to control purchase limits without a code change, creating both a delivery risk and an operational gap.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. A `maxOrderQuantity` site preference exists in Business Manager, editable by merchandisers without a deployment.
2. The default value is `3` and the field enforces a minimum of `1`.
3. The resolved value (product-level if set, site preference as fallback) is returned on the SCAPI product response as `c_maxOrderQuantity` and is consumable by the PWA Kit.
4. When no product-level override exists, the site preference value is returned. When a product-level override exists (SFCC-703), it takes precedence.

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Storefront architecture | Headless PWA Kit. No cartridge-rendered storefront. All product data is consumed via SCAPI (Shopper Products API). |
| Merchandiser access | The configuration must be updatable in Business Manager without a code deployment. |
| Storefront scope | Solution must work across all storefronts (AU, UK, US Dom, US Intl, EU, ME). The site preference is per-site, supporting independent configuration per storefront. |
| Enforcement scope | This ticket covers configuration only. PDP enforcement is SFCC-196; Cart enforcement is SFCC-250; per-product/customer-group overrides are SFCC-703. |

### 2.2 Assumptions

| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| PWA Kit consumes product data via SCAPI Shopper Products API (`/shopper/products/v1/products/{id}`). | If OCAPI is used instead, the extension point changes from a SCAPI hook to an OCAPI `afterGET` hook — see Section 3 for both options. |
| Custom attributes prefixed `c_` on the SCAPI product response are already enabled for the site via the endpoint configuration. | If not enabled, `c_maxOrderQuantity` will not appear in the response and the PWA will always fall back to the hardcoded default. |
| SFCC-703 (per-product `maxOrderQuantity` custom attribute) will be implemented after this ticket. The resolution logic in this ticket must accommodate it when ready. | If 703 is built without aligning on the custom attribute name and resolution order, enforcement logic in SFCC-196 and SFCC-250 will need rework. |
| The agreed default value is `3`. | If the business default changes, the site preference value in BM must be updated; the code default is a safety net only. |

---

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Option A** — SCAPI Hook (`dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` on SCAPI endpoint) | + Resolution logic is server-side, not duplicated in the PWA + Single response field (`c_maxOrderQuantity`) for consumers to read + SFCC-703 override handled at hook layer with no PWA changes required | - Requires SCAPI custom hook registration and cartridge configuration - Hook fires on every product GET; negligible but non-zero overhead | Yes — Recommended |
| **Option B** — OCAPI Hook (`dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` on OCAPI endpoint) | + Same resolution logic as Option A + Familiar pattern if OCAPI is already in use | - Only valid if PWA Kit is consuming OCAPI Shop API, not SCAPI — PWA Kit default is SCAPI - Mixing OCAPI and SCAPI introduces dual maintenance overhead | Yes — if OCAPI confirmed |
| **Option C** — Separate MRT API route fetching site preference independently | + Keeps product response clean | - Additional network round trip on every product page load - Config fetch must be coordinated with product fetch, adding complexity to PWA state management - Not necessary when hook approach cleanly solves the problem | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A — SCAPI Hook (Recommended)

A SCAPI product hook intercepts the `GET /shopper/products/v1/products/{id}` response server-side. The hook reads the product's custom attribute `maxOrderQuantity` (set per SFCC-703) and falls back to the `maxOrderQuantity` site preference (set per this ticket). The resolved value is written to `c_maxOrderQuantity` on the response object. The PWA reads a single consistent field with no resolution logic client-side.

#### Option B — OCAPI Hook

Functionally identical to Option A but targets the OCAPI Shop API product endpoint instead of SCAPI. Only applicable if the PWA Kit implementation has been configured to use OCAPI for product data rather than SCAPI. The hook pattern and resolution logic are the same; only the registration target differs.

#### Option C — Separate MRT API Route (Discarded)

Discarded — introduces an additional network dependency on every product page load and requires the PWA to coordinate two async responses, adding complexity that is entirely avoidable with the hook approach.

---

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A — SCAPI Hook**

### 4.2 Rationale

The SCAPI hook places all resolution logic server-side, meaning the PWA Kit only ever reads a single field (`c_maxOrderQuantity`) with no branching logic. This keeps SFCC-196 and SFCC-250 simple to implement and ensures SFCC-703's per-product override is handled transparently at the hook layer without any future PWA changes. It is consistent with how other custom product attributes are extended in a headless SFCC setup.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

The hook fires on every product GET request. The overhead is negligible (one site preference read + one attribute check), but it is a non-zero addition to every product response. This is accepted given the simplification it provides to all downstream consumers.

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence

1. Merchandiser sets `maxOrderQuantity` in Business Manager under **Merchant Tools → Site Preferences → Custom Preferences**.
2. Shopper navigates to a PDP or cart; PWA Kit calls SCAPI `GET /shopper/products/v1/products/{id}`.
3. SCAPI hook fires on the product response.
4. Hook checks `product.custom.maxOrderQuantity`: if set and greater than 0, uses the product-level value (SFCC-703 override).
5. If no product-level value, hook reads `Site.getCurrent().getPreferenceValue('maxOrderQuantity')`.

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |

### 7. Building against absent data

#### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

#### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

#### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

### 11. Signposts in the repo that point at nothing

Each of these has already cost time.

- **`overrides.md` does not exist.** `overrideStyling.md:4,112,179` references it three times
  and positions it as the companion doc defining module-replacement correctness. It exists only
  on two unmerged spike branches.

  (`grep -c` → 0). `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest omits it, along with `css.md`,
  `components.md`, `typescript.md` and `tagging.md` — three of which are in `conventions.md`'s
  own "See also" list. The largest rules file, holding the entire styling hierarchy, is
  invisible to Cursor and Copilot.
- **The rules set is split on its own component convention.** `components.md` and
  `conventions.md` contain **zero** occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or

  `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself — `:136` cites the correct
  `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` while `:130`/`:139` prescribe a
  `components/custom/` directory that has never existed.

  has ever been created.

  **zero** of squadB's 9 do. Both instruct edits to files not in the repo, and both were last
  touched 2026-07-14. And they contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership —
  CODEOWNERS says Squad B and is the one that enforces.
- **`sprintScope.md` is two months stale** and `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule 14 makes it load-bearing
  for scoping. It says "Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)" while its own table puts today in
  Sprint 5. Applied literally it would classify current PDP work as past-sprint.
- **`.docs/architecture.md` misstates the stack**: React Router v6 (actually 5.3.4 — the
  footer uses `useHistory`), Storybook 8 (actually 10.4.6), axe via `vitest-axe`/`axe-playwright`
  (neither installed), Playwright "not yet configured" (7 projects, two workflows), "all
  services mocked (MSW stubs)" — `msw@1.3.5` is present transitively but has zero references in
  `overrides/`, and it is a test tool, not a local-dev data source. (`AGENTS.md` bans MSW in
  *production paths* only; `testing.md` permits it for integration tests.)
- **`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`** (`overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53` — note the top-level
  `config/` is a different, Tier 1 directory) has zero consumers and duplicates
  `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`.
- **`connectionPools.ts` looks like live infrastructure and is dead code** — `ssr.js` doesn't
  import it. The blast-radius isolation its header claims is not in effect.

**The pattern:** trust the code, `CODEOWNERS`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, and `tagging.md`.
Verify everything else before citing it. A rules file's worked example is as likely to describe
an unmerged branch as the one you're on.

content.text:
**Phase 5 — handoff. Verdict: 🔴 BLOCKED.** I stopped at the gate and did not run `/feature-spec`, `/scope-check` or `zm-planner` — writing a scoped prompt on top of the contradiction below would have produced a plan for the wrong build.

## The one that matters

**The ticket describes a PDP that doesn't exist yet.**

SFCC-196 says: *"Since the PDP has no quantity selector, enforcement is triggered when a shopper clicks Add to Bag multiple times for the same size."* The entire mechanism rests on that sentence.

But [product-view/index.tsx:862](overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:862) renders a `QuantityPicker` right now, unconditionally — it's only skipped for sets and bundles. It even carries an `audit-allow` comment saying it's verbatim from base and copy-first requires it unchanged.

So if we build exactly what the ticket asks for, a shopper sets the picker to 5, clicks Add to Bag **once**, and walks straight past the limit. Click-counting only works if there's nothing else to count with. The attached design confirms it — no picker anywhere in it.

## The rest of the gate

Two more blockers, then things we can plan around:

| | Finding |
|---|---|
| 🔴 | **No Figma node.** Ticket says "Figma is leading" but only has a PNG, and an annotation dot sits on top of the error copy. The design system has **no** inline-error component at all, so there's nothing to reuse. SFCC-211 ("ask Charmaine to design error messaging") is `Done`, so it exists — I just can't reach it. |
| 🔴 | **No acceptance criteria, and it's not DoR-complete.** The description is narrative only. **Automation for Jira bounced it on 26 Aug** — *"All DoR checklist items must be completed before moving this issue forward"* — yet the status still says `Ready for Development`. Nothing here is testable as written. |
| 🟡 | **TSD-SFCC-268 is Draft, unsigned**, author and reviewer are literal `[Name]` placeholders. It's the *only* definition of the `c_maxOrderQuantity` contract we'd consume. SFCC-268 is `Ready to deploy to UAT` so the work looks done — but the doc says it isn't approved. |
| 🟡 | That TSD also tells us to extend `app/hooks/useProduct.js`. **That file doesn't exist** in retail-react-app v10 — `useProduct` comes from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`. Contract's fine, file path is wrong. |
| 🟡 | **`c_maxOrderQuantity` appears nowhere in the repo** and I couldn't confirm it's live — `healthCheckAll.sh` skipped all three endpoints (no URLs in `.env.local`). |
| 🟡 | **PRD conflict.** `.docs/prd/pdp.md:52` says the limit is *per customer group* (PRD-011, "confirmed") — but refinement moved that to SFCC-703 on 11 Aug. That line is stale. §6 of the same file says *"Max 3 units per SKU… (CAI-017, confirmed)"*, which does match. **CAI-017 is the requirement to cite**, not PRD-011. |

Two governance notes worth your attention separately: `overrides/app/components/product-view/` has **no CODEOWNERS entry and there's no default `*` rule**, so a shared component that base `cart`, `wishlist` and both product modals all resolve into currently needs zero owner review. And the good news — `zimmTextInput` already has the exact inline-error pattern to reuse (`role="alert"`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`), and `text.error` `#9c0000` measures 8.7:1 on white, so accessibility is not a risk here.

content.text:
That changes my recommendation. **SFCC-650's own description resolves the contradiction** — I should have read it before framing the question that way.

> *"...size selection validation, stock state awareness, loading state during cart API call, and **inline error messaging**. Cart API integration is in scope for this story. **Maximum purchase quantity enforcement is handled separately in SFCC-196.**"*

So this was never meant to be one piece of work. The design screenshot I showed you actually spans **three** tickets:

| Ticket | Owns | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-648** `pdp/size-selector` | the size dropdown | To Do, **High** |
| **SFCC-650** `pdp/add-to-bag` | the CTA, cart API integration, **the inline error message itself** | To Do, **High** |
| **SFCC-196** (this one) | the max-quantity **rule** only | Ready for Dev, Medium |

SFCC-196 was scoped *assuming 650 already exists*. That's why its description says "the PDP has no quantity selector" — it's describing the PDP **after** 648/650 land, not the one we have. The ticket isn't wrong; it's just ahead of its dependencies.

Two more things that firm this up:

- **The PRD never mentions a quantity picker on PDP.** I grepped all of `.docs/prd/` — nothing. §6 describes per-size availability and *"Max 3 units per SKU… enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017)"*. The `QuantityPicker` currently rendering is inherited Salesforce scaffolding that nobody has removed yet. It's destined to go — but under 648/650's redesign, not ours.
- **Correction to what I said earlier on blast radius.** I implied base `cart` and `wishlist` import `product-view` directly. They don't — they import `product-view-modal`, which imports it. Our override still renders inside those modals, so the exposure is real, but it's one level indirect rather than a direct import.

## Where that leaves us

Option (b) — remove the picker and click-count — is now clearly wrong. We'd be doing 648 and 650's work, and we'd be doing it inside `product-view`, which 650 is going to replace with a purpose-built component anyway.

Option (a) — cap the picker — builds UI against a control that's scheduled for deletion. Cheap, but it's throwaway.

**My recommendation is (c), re-sequenced — with a caveat, because I don't think you should hand the sprint slot back empty.**

There's a genuinely independent slice of SFCC-196 that survives whatever 650 builds, because it's pure logic with no UI:

1. Read `c_maxOrderQuantity` off the product response, with the safety-net fallback of 3 (per the TSD contract).
2. A selector that counts units of a given variant already in the basket, off `useCurrentBasket`.
3. A pure `canAddToBag(variantId, requestedQty, maxQty, basket)` function plus Vitest coverage.

That's the entire *rule*. It's what 650 would then call. It doesn't touch `product-view`, doesn't need the Figma node, and doesn't depend on which size control ships — so two of my three blockers stop applying to it. The third (no ACs) I'd still want Jasmijn to close, but the behaviour here is specified well enough by CAI-017 and the TSD to write tests against.

Before I'd commit to even that, one thing needs verifying: **is `c_maxOrderQuantity` actually on the SCAPI response in dev or SIT?** SFCC-268 says `Ready to deploy to UAT`, but I couldn't confirm it — every health-check endpoint skipped for want of a URL in `.env.local`. If that field isn't live, even the logic slice is building against a contract nobody has proven.

What's your read — does the thin logic slice appeal, or would you rather park 196 entirely and push 648/650 up the queue?
